text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- EU Commissioner Karel Van Miert says he will demand that Credit Lyonnais implement large asset sales in France, on top of foreign assets, before the EU clears further subsidies for the state-owned bank. He says French state help to the textile sector distorts European competition.
-- National statistics office INSEE survey finds households worried about rising unemployment and flat buying power, savings accounts for rise in household consumption expected for Q2.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe calls firms to adopt shorter work hours to avoid job cuts.
-- Bouygues to ally with Italian STET in mobile telephone activity, enter capital of SNCF state-owned rail operator's telecom subsidiary.
-- UAP insurer reduces to 10 percent its 30 percent stake in reinsurer Scor.
-- Matra reaffirms interest for Aerospatiale missile and satellite activity.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- COE economic studies centre says sales in large retail stores fell 9.3 percent from August, households depressed, firms' investment sluggish.
-- Tour operator Nouvelles Frontieres chairman Jacques Maillot reaffirms interest in buying Air Liberte.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- INSEE confirms economic growth fell 0.4 percent in the second quarter, revises down slightly 1996 yearly growth to 1.2 percent.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis calls local authorities to share spending cuts efforts.
-- Studies show consumption remains stronger than what could be expected in view of the current historic low of French household morale.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade says there will be no talk of privatisation until mid-1998.
-- New Caledonia separatists call for ownership of nickel mining area controlled by mining group Eramet.
L'AGEFI

Investment funds Wyser Pratte & Co and Verneuil Finance have nine percent of tools and office furniture group Strafor Facom, paper says, quoting an informed source. The funds have officially said their stake is 6.11 percent. A "spin-off" would value the share at 650 francs, paper says.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- French lawmakers propose higher tax on fast food to protect old-fashioned bistros and raise revenue.
